question: How much carbon sink does the Revised Green India Mission (GIM) Plan released in 2025 aim to create by 2030?
solution:
The correct answer is __**3.39 billion tonnes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Revised Green India Mission (GIM) Plan**, released in **2025**, aims to create a **carbon sink of 3.39 billion tonnes** by **2030**.
 
• The Green India Mission is one of the **eight national missions** under the **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)** launched by the Government of India in **2010**.
 
• This mission focuses on **afforestation, reforestation, and ecosystem restoration** to enhance carbon sequestration and mitigate climate change.
 
• The target of **3.39 billion tonnes** aligns with India's commitments under the **Paris Agreement** to reduce **greenhouse gas emissions** and increase forest and tree cover.
 
• The mission emphasizes the involvement of local communities, especially in rural areas, to ensure sustainable development and environmental conservation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Green India Mission (GIM):**

 
 
• The Green India Mission was launched as part of India's response to **climate change adaptation and mitigation**.
 
• It aims to increase **forest/tree cover by 5 million hectares** and improve the quality of existing forest cover on **5 million hectares**.
 
• The mission includes activities like **ecosystem restoration, biodiversity conservation, and livelihood enhancement** for forest-dependent communities.
 
 
 
• **Carbon Sink:**
 
 
• A **carbon sink** refers to any system that absorbs more carbon dioxide than it emits. Examples include **forests, oceans, and soil**.
 
• By increasing forest cover and improving vegetation, the Green India Mission contributes to enhancing India's **natural carbon sinks**.
 
• This process helps in reducing the concentration of **CO2** in the atmosphere, thereby combating global warming.
 
 
 
• **Paris Agreement:**
 
 
• India is a signatory to the **Paris Agreement**, adopted in **2015**, which seeks to limit global temperature rise to **below 2°C**.
 
• Under its **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)**, India has committed to increasing its forest cover to help mitigate climate change.
 
 
 
• **Community Participation:**
 
 
• The Green India Mission encourages the active involvement of **local communities, panchayats, and NGOs** in afforestation and conservation projects.
 
• These efforts contribute to **sustainable rural development**, providing livelihoods to forest-dependent populations while ensuring ecological balance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Afforestation Targets:** The Green India Mission sets specific targets for **afforestation** and **reforestation** projects to enhance carbon sequestration.
 
• **Ecosystem Services:** The mission aims to improve **ecosystem services**, including water conservation, soil fertility, and biodiversity preservation.
 
• **Monitoring Mechanisms:** Advanced technologies like **GIS mapping** and remote sensing are employed to monitor progress and ensure accountability.
 
• **Climate Resilience:** The initiative also focuses on building **climate-resilient ecosystems** to minimize the adverse effects of climate change.
 
• **Budget Allocation:** Significant financial resources are allocated to achieve the mission's objectives effectively, with the support of **state governments and international organizations**.
